Out-of-bounds read: accessing memory outside an array's allocated range, usually via an unchecked index.
The standard binary format for floating-point numbers, used by almost every language's float/double type.
Set-user-ID: a file permission bit that runs a program as its owner (often root) instead of the invoking user.
A syscall that changes a process's apparent root directory, used to sandbox or jail it.
Segmentation fault: a crash caused by accessing memory the process isn't allowed to touch.
A search that halves the remaining range each step, needing only log2(N) probes to pin down a value.
In an exploit, anything that answers a single yes/no question about hidden state, one query at a time.
A byte order where the least-significant byte is stored first.
A random value placed before a return address; if overwritten by a buffer overflow, the program detects it and aborts.
Trusted Platform Module: a chip (or emulated component) that stores keys and attests to system state.
Return-oriented programming: chaining existing code fragments (gadgets) via the stack to execute arbitrary logic without injecting new code.
Address Space Layout Randomization: randomizes memory addresses each run to make exploits harder to write reliably.
